billing.multi_team: user-level capability — any user may be a member of N teams (rate-limited creation for abuse); each team independently selects its plan. NOT a tier feature.

storage._comment: #11758 — the TWO purchasable storage dimensions (owner 'ok', 2026-11-08, issue comment 6807826749). Each tier includes an amount (tiers.<t>.max_postgres_storage_bytes / tiers.<t>.max_graph_storage_mb); above it the customer buys more at the rate below. The allowance and the bill are PER ACCOUNT: a second graph does not double the allowance and adds no second line. ⛔ There is deliberately NO per-graph and NO per-node allowance anywhere in this block: nodes were retired as the customer-facing pricing unit (#4495/#5331 — 'the node cap is replaced, not extended'), and the owner's correction on #11758 (comment 6805077325) is explicit that the storage shape is 'per account only'. ⚠ THIS BLOCK DOES NOT CHANGE GRAPH COUNTS. free=1 and solo=2 remain, and pro/team remain unlimited (owner decision, Gate #2, 2026-09-01) — 'nothing per graph' is about what is PRICED, not about how many graphs a tier may create.

postgres_storage.label: stored data
postgres_storage.market_anchor: Pinecone $0.33/GB-month, Neon $0.35/GB-month (the two closest comparables) — #11758 comment 6807281064

graph_storage.label: hot capacity
graph_storage.market_anchor: Neo4j Aura ~$87.6 per GB of hot DATA ($65.70 per PROVISIONED GB x 1.33), FalkorDB ~$97 — #11758 comment 6807281064
graph_storage.unit_trap: The market quotes PROVISIONED RAM; a customer buys DATA HELD HOT, and 1 GB of data needs 1.33 GB provisioned (75% usable rule). Our cost is $43.75 provisioned / 0.75 = $58.33 per GB of hot DATA. The market's effective rate per GB of hot data is 65.70 x 1.33 = $87.6. Comparing our $85 to the market's $65.70/GB drops the 1.33 and makes us look ~29% ABOVE market when we are ~3% BELOW it; the market figure itself is understated by a quarter (65.70 vs 87.6).

storage.gb_definition: 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes = 1,000 decimal MB (the `bytes_per_gb` field above is the same number NUMERICALLY, so the code constant and this artifact can be asserted equal rather than compared as prose). Pinned here because the two meters publish DIFFERENT units (postgres_storage in bytes, graph_storage in decimal MB) and a silent MiB/decimal mix is the measured 3.59x error class in docs/architecture/STORAGE-ARCHITECTURE.md. One definition, one conversion, no per-caller factor.
storage._included_amounts_status: DERIVED, NOT OWNER-CONFIRMED. The per-tier included amounts are computed from the owner's 30%-of-price rule (docs/architecture/SEARCH-ARCHITECTURE.md section 8: solo $19 -> $5.70 budget -> ~77 MB hot window + ~1 GB record; pro/team rows are that document's generalisation of the rule, not a ruling on those tiers) and the rates above are set, but the OWNER has NOT confirmed the included amounts — #11758 comment 6807826749 lists them as explicitly NOT decided ('a product choice, not implied by the rates'). They are defaults of record, pending. Free/anon are the exception: hot capacity 0 is stated by the decision record; the included stored-data amount is 'small' with no number given, so it is null (= unconfigured = unlimited, which is today's behaviour) rather than an invented figure.
storage._per_graph_overhead: NOT priced here. Per-graph fixed overhead (FalkorDB pre-allocates NODE_CREATION_BUFFER = 16,384 node slots per graph) is unmeasured and is OUR cost inside the 30%, not a customer-facing control; if it proves material the answer is an accounting floor counted into the account total, never a cap and never a per-graph control (#10743).

billing.integrations: unlimited at ALL tiers — more integrations = more usage = more value; abuse controlled by connection rate-limit, not tier caps
